About Patronus AI

Patronus AI is a frontier lab developing simulation research and infrastructure to accelerate progress toward human-aligned AGI. We are on a mission to simulate all of the world’s intelligence.

At a glance

• Engagement: Independent contractor, fully remote

• Pay: $50 - $125/hr

• Start: Rolling

• Location: Remote

• Team: Talent Acquisition

The role
The data behind our work is produced by practicing domain experts on contract: Unreal engineers who ship games, software engineers, and specialists in whatever domain a customer needs next. We are hiring Growth Associates to find those people and get them into the funnel, across one to three domains each.
This is not a volume seat. Every expert you put forward sits a screener written by the people who will review their work, and you are measured on how many of them pass it rather than on how many you sent. A large pipeline that fails the screener is a bad week.
The people worth finding are rarely applying. They are shipping, and the evidence that they are good is public: commits, credits, talks, papers, answers in the forums their peers read. Your job is to read that evidence and start a conversation that someone with a job they like will reply to.
What you'll do

• Hit a weekly target for qualified experts added, by domain, set with the Internal Strategic Projects Lead running the project.

• Find people doing the work now rather than people who did it once. In game development that means shipped credits and current engine versions, not a decade-old title.

• Work the venues these people actually use: GitHub, engine and framework forums, Discord servers, conference speaker lists, studio credits, paper author lists, specialist job boards. LinkedIn is one channel out of several.

• Write outreach that survives contact with a senior engineer who is not looking.

• Hand off clean. Every expert reaches the funnel with their domain, seniority and the evidence behind both, so nobody has to re-research them.

• Tell us what the market is telling you. If a domain is not there at the rate we want, we would rather hear it in week one.

• Use AI aggressively. Market mapping, research, outreach drafting and funnel analysis should all be automated as far as they can be, so your hours go to the judgment calls.

Who we're looking for
Required

• Three or more years sourcing technical or specialist talent, including at least one hard pool you can describe in detail: who they were, where you found them, why that worked.

• A method you can explain without naming LinkedIn Recruiter. Where do these people gather, how did you work that out, what got you a reply.

• You can name the last five people you found who were not applying and not on the first page of results.

• Enough technical fluency to read a GitHub profile, a set of game credits or a paper and form your own view of whether the experience is real or adjacent.

• You build your own tooling. Scripts, automations, enrichment, prompts. Tell us about something you assembled rather than something you subscribe to.

• You are comfortable being measured on whether your candidates pass.

• Clear, precise writing in professional English. Your outreach is the first thing an expert reads about us.

• Ability to work independently and asynchronously against deadlines.

Nice to have

• Sourcing for professional knowledge work for a marketplace or contingent workforce at volume.

• Experience sourcing against a quality gate someone

This position will be on-site in Idaho Falls, Idaho.

Position Description

Oklo Isotopes is building scalable U.S. radioisotope production capabilities in facilities dedicated to producing essential isotopes for healthcare, space, industry, research, and defense applications. In February 2026, Oklo’s Idaho Radioisotopes Laboratory (IRL) located in Idaho Falls received its Material Possession License from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to take a leading role in the manufacturing and distribution of beneficial radioisotopes in the U.S.

We are seeking a Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) to serve as the technical authority for radiation protection activities at the IRL. This role is designed for an experienced Certified Health Physicist (CHP) or an equivalently seasoned radiation protection professional who brings strong technical judgment, operational leadership, and deep expertise in radiation safety program implementation.

• Bachelor’s degree in Health Physics, Nuclear Engineering, Radiochemistry, Chemistry, Physics, or a related technical discipline.

title: Linux Kernel Live Patching Engineer
description:
About Sardina Systems

Sardina Systems builds cloud infrastructure software based on OpenStack, Kubernetes, and Ceph for cloud operators, enterprises, and service providers across the globe. Behind our technology is a distributed team of builders creating reliable systems for our users.
Position summary
Build and operate a live kernel patching feed for AlmaLinux 10. You own the full technical chain, from CVE triage to signed, tested RPMs published in a public repository. This is a hands-on kernel engineering role, not a management or release-coordination position.
Core responsibilities
Patch engineering

• Track AlmaLinux security advisories (ALSA) and upstream kernel CVEs.

• Triage CVEs against the published scope: critical, remotely exploitable or actively exploited vulnerabilities.

• Backport security fixes to the supported AlmaLinux 10 kernels, resolving conflicts across version differences.

• Generate live patch modules with klp-build. Initially, publish individual CVE patches; evaluate cumulative/atomic replace strategies as the pipeline matures.

• Identify CVEs that cannot be live patched (e.g. __init changes, data structure layout changes) and record them in the coverage-gap log.

Build and distribution pipeline

• Reproduce AlmaLinux kernel builds exactly (same source, config and compiler), e.g. in mock with the AlmaLinux buildroot, so modules match the running kernel.

• Maintain the automated pipeline: CVE scan, build plan, klp-build, RPM packaging, signing, test gate, createrepo_c publication.

• Plan and execute the move of support to new AlmaLinux kernel releases as they ship.

• Verify the exact client-side commands work on stock AlmaLinux 10 (dnf kpatch auto plus kpatch-patch-* packages).

Testing and release gate

• Run the mandatory pre-publication gate on every patch:

• load and unload on the target kernel in QEMU;

- run kernel livepatch selftests;

• for high-severity CVEs: apply and revert under load on a FishOS test cluster with running VMs and Ceph I/O.

• Document which tests were passed for each release.

• A patch that passes the gate is cleared for publication. Do not publish a patch that has failed the gate.

Release and withdrawal

• Publish approved patches with release notes listing the CVEs covered.

• Publish the source for every released patch alongside its RPM.

• If a published patch misbehaves: pull it from the repository, publish an advisory, and give users revert instructions.

• Maintain the runbook and coverage-gap log.

Secure Boot

• Manage the Sardina module-signing key and RPM signing key.

• Document and verify mokutil key enrolment for AlmaLinux users.

• Work with the Ops team to automate key enrolment on FishOS.

Required skills

• Linux kernel development: strong C, with hands-on experience backporting kernel patches or debugging kernel modules. Screening will test this directly.

• Live patching: practical experience with klp-build or kpatch, or demonstrated ability to learn them quickly from source.

• RPM and the RHEL/AlmaLinux ecosystem: kernel packaging (RPM/SRPM), mock, dnf, createrepo_c and repository metadata.

• Automation: Python or shell; building and maintaining CI-style pipelines.

• Signing: GPG key management and RPM signing; kernel module signature verification and MOK enrolment.

- English: working proficiency.
Preferred skills

• Spoken Russian and/or Mandarin, in addition to English. This is to work closely with Russian- and Mandarin-speaking team members.

• QEMU-based VM validation or canary testing.

• Upstream kernel contributions or involvement in the live patching community.

• Koji or similar build orchestration systems.

• Ceph I/O testing or storage-heavy workloads.

Key traits

• Boundary awareness: Willing to say plainly "this CVE needs a reboot" and "this kernel is out of scope" rather than forcing a risky patch

• Release discipline: Understands that a bad patch is the main reputational risk and will not skip the test gate under pressure
